To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we synthesized new anthracycline derivatives with a trisaccharidic aglycone and found that 3"-O-acyl derivatives of daunorubicin trisaccharides have potent antitumor activity.

we have synthesized new anthracycline derivatives having the trisacerharide and have found that 3"-O-acyl derivatives of daunorubicin, carminomycins and aklavinones showed a marked antineoplastic activity.
we synthesized a series of new anthradycline antibiotics with trisacchardies and found that their antitumor activities were markedly potent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new series of anthracycline antibiotics with the trisacchloride.
the development of a new type of antitumor agents, anthracycline glycosides, which are expected to be more active than their aglycones.
the chemical modification of anthradycline antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
3"-O-acyl derivatives of anthracyclones glycosides are more effective than the corresponding deacylated ones in the L1210 leukemia test.
the trisaccharyl derivatives of anthracyclones are not superior in antitumor activity and toxicity to the corresponding monosaccharide derivatives.

the glycosidation of the aglycones with the trisacchride, which was prepared by the glycosidations of O-alpha-L-rhodosyl-(1 leads 4)-O-alpha-L-fucopyranosyl with O-(3-O-acetly-2-deoxy- alpha-L-cineruloside, gave the most active anthracycline antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3"-O-acyl derivatives of daunamycinone, carimomycinone and the glycosides of these aglycons showed a marked activity against L121O leukemia.
the glycosidation product of 3"-O-deacetyladriamycincinone with trisacchride is a potent antitumor agent.
the 3"-OH group of anthracycline antibiotics has a crucial effect on the antitumor activity of the glycosides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glycosidation of anthracyclones with trisacchride and the deacylation of the products resulted in the synthesis of anthracylines having trisaccharides.
the trisacchardie is a promising new glycosyl residue for anthracycline derivatives.

the glycosylation at 3-OH position of the anthracycline aglycones with the trisacchride, O-alpha-L-cimerulosyl-(1 to 4)- O-(3-O-acety-2-deoxy-a-L-fucoside) (1 to 4) -a, b-L-rhodosaminide, is a very important factor for increasing antitumor activity.
